answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits confirm fraud. Auditors are randomly assigned and rewarded for catching defects, so creating many names does not create many trusted votes; each new identity needs fresh capital and risks losing it. The ivory, jade, and falcon agents can all join, but none gets influence merely by multiplying its identities.
